assistant:
You’re right that **c8 flips two discs now** — but in the endgame, that can be a trap.

Before choosing it, ask: **after Black plays c8, what strong White move appears on the bottom-left edge?** In particular, look at the empty corner area around **a8/b8/c8**. Moves next to corners/edges can decide the final count more than the immediate flips.

So: don’t judge c8 by “2 flips”; judge it by **what it lets White do next**.

user: So if I played A1, it would essentially freeze row 1 and column H, right, since neither of us would be able to flip anything in those rows/columns?
assistant:
Almost — but two corrections:

- **a1 isn’t a legal Black move right now** (no pale dot there).
- If you *could* take **a1**, the **a1 corner disc itself is permanent**, but it doesn’t “freeze row 1 and column h.” It affects **row 1 and column a**.

Also, row 1 would **not** be frozen for Black here: with **a1 black** and **b1–g1 white**, if Black later got **h1**, those whites on row 1 could flip to Black. So corners are permanent, but the whole edge becomes stable only when it’s connected/secured.

user: Why do some of these squares not have the white dot that makes them eligible for play?
assistant:
A square is legal only if placing a Black disc there would **trap at least one straight line of White discs** between the new Black disc and an existing Black disc.

Straight lines can be horizontal, vertical, or diagonal.

Example: **c8** is legal because along the diagonal upward-right you’d have **d7 White, e6 White**, then **f5 Black** — so those Whites would flip.

A square without a pale dot has no such “White(s) in a row ending at Black” line, so Black can’t play there.

user: Okay, so a move MUST trap at least one opponent disc?
assistant:
Yes. In Othello, you may only play on an empty square if it **flanks/traps at least one opponent disc** in a straight line — horizontal, vertical, or diagonal — with one of your discs on the far end.

That’s why only **g2, b6, a7, b7, b8, c8** are legal for Black here. If a square doesn’t flip at least one White disc, you can’t play there.
